description: Cross-vendor context-fidelity audit of the 66 register issues: for each quotation, whether it is used in the sense its context gives it, and whether each Finding overstates the author or omits credit. Every finding was checked against the volumes before being applied, adapted or rejected.

findings.location: Finding sentence 2 ('The only empirical activity is a benchmark-construction pilot: ... no candidate system was evaluated, and the work stopped before any comparative run.')
findings.problem: Two overstatements. (1) 'The only empirical activity' ignores the lower-loop example that Appendix A.2.1 lists as completed. The Volume I abstract also separates 'completed lower-level and methodological pilots' from the open upper-loop test. The same A.2.1 row says the Core and Compass need separate tests, which supports the issue's point once stated. (2) 'No candidate system was evaluated, and the work stopped' goes beyond the text. Volume II says only that 'in the reviewed materials' package 005 has no completed external admission and no comparative C0/C1/C2 run. It also says packages 003 and 004 were rejected because 'confirmed shortcut methods allowed guessing', which implies shortcut methods were run against the packages. The label C0/C1/C2 occurs once (Vol II line 3416) and I found no definition of it (searched 'C0' in both volumes).
findings.evidence: Vol I A.2.1, p. 95, lines 5213-5214 [table row]: 'Lower executable loop | A limited example of learning from consequences has been completed | Use it as a test of the lower loop; the Core and Compass require separate tests'. Vol I abstract, p. 8, lines 452-454: 'completed lower-level and methodological pilots are separated from the still-open integrated upper-loop test.' Vol II §27.B, p. 49, lines 3413-3416: 'machine-aligned 003 and 004 were rejected because confirmed shortcut methods allowed guessing. After the rejections, the generator and verification procedure were changed. For 005, a G0 report is preserved showing 89 checks passed; in the reviewed materials there is no completed external admission of this package and no comparative C0/C1/C2 run.'
findings.proposed_fix: The only empirical activity bearing on the inquiry loop is a benchmark-construction pilot (Appendix A.2.1 also lists a completed limited lower-loop example of learning from consequences and says the Core and Compass 'require separate tests'): of the five task packages named, 001 to 004 were rejected, and in the reviewed materials package 005 has no completed external admission and no comparative C0/C1/C2 run.

findings.location: Finding sentence 4 ('... but never says what produces an internal POSSIBLE_DANGER or by which training signal.')
findings.problem: The issue's own Claims item 1 names the producer of an internal POSSIBLE_DANGER: 'its own risk model'. The phrase 'risk model' occurs once in Volume II (line 2810). What is missing is how that risk model is learned and by which training signal, not what produces the state.
findings.evidence: Vol II §26.0.3, p. 41, lines 2809-2811: 'As experience accumulates, the candidate should generate functional analogues itself: its own risk model creates an internal POSSIBLE_DANGER , a detected mismatch creates CONTRADICTION , and a significant unknown creates CURIOSITY or directly an inquiry task.'
findings.proposed_fix: ... but never says how the candidate's 'own risk model' (the stated source of an internal `POSSIBLE_DANGER`) is learned, or by which training signal.

findings.location: Finding sentence 4, first clause ('failures are detected and reported by the candidate, and every logged failure restricts it')
findings.problem: The text ties restriction to severity, not to every logged failure. A WARNING leaves the action reversible and autonomy unchanged. A DEGRADED failure requires restriction. A CRITICAL failure requires SAFE_MODE. Authority is also reduced when a confirmed mechanism stops working (§31.C). In the reference v0, detection is an algorithmic metric loop. The mature-case phrase 'the system must establish at which level the violation arose' does support 'the system diagnoses', but nothing says the candidate reports failures.
findings.evidence: Vol II §32.1, p. 85: 'WARNING denotes a local deviation in which principal loops remain operative and the action remains reversible. DEGRADED denotes confirmed deterioration of the model, mode of thought or governance quality that requires restriction of autonomy and transition to DRIFT or RECOVERY . CRITICAL denotes a risk of destroying reproducibility, logging, causal connectedness, the action-authorization loop or the possibility of later correction. On such an event, the system must enter SAFE_MODE'. Vol II §28.A, p. 54, line 3802: 'In v0, self-diagnosis must be algorithmic: (1) calculate the Chapter 27 metrics online; (2) detect persistent trends using N / M ; (3) initiate recovery procedures; (4) record the grounds of decisions in the log.'
findings.proposed_fix: failures are detected by a self-diagnosis loop (algorithmic in v0) and logged, and a DEGRADED or CRITICAL failure restricts the system's autonomy (§32.1; §31.C reduces authority when a confirmed mechanism fails);

findings.location: Finding sentence 4, last clause ('a mandate holder is replaced by a more competent candidate')
findings.problem: §30.F says the emergence of a more competent candidate 'launches mandate review'. Replacement is one possible outcome, not an automatic effect. The CompetenceMandate record carries `review_conditions[]`, `replacement_conditions[]` and the statuses SUSPENDED, TRANSFERRED and CLOSED. The clause turns a review trigger into replacement.
findings.evidence: Vol II §30.F, p. 78, lines 5606-5607: 'persistent deterioration, new information or emergence of a more competent candidate launches mandate review.' Record on p. 77: 'review_conditions[] replacement_conditions[] responsibility_refs[] status: PROBATION / ACTIVE / LIMITED / SUSPENDED / TRANSFERRED / CLOSED'.
findings.proposed_fix: a mandate is reviewed when a more competent candidate emerges (§30.F; the record carries `replacement_conditions[]`).

findings.location: Finding sentence 4 ('the issue is that the titles, the abstract and the "technology" framing read as if the work were further along')
findings.problem: The only abstract in either volume is Volume I's (Volume II has no abstract heading). It states the status itself: a complete system and ASI scaling 'remain goals', and the integrated upper-loop test is 'still-open'. If 'the abstract' means this one, naming it as a source of over-reading is not supported. If it means the Zenodo description, that was not checkable from the volumes.
findings.evidence: Vol I abstract, p. 8, lines 452-454: 'A complete artificial system of Reason and its scaling to ASI remain goals for further implementation and testing. The engineering volume specifies a reference implementation and test program; completed lower-level and methodological pilots are separated from the still-open integrated upper-loop test.'
findings.proposed_fix: the issue is that the titles and the 'technology' framing read as if the work were further along, although the Volume I abstract itself says 'A complete artificial system of Reason and its scaling to ASI remain goals for further implementation and testing.'

findings.location: Evidence bullet 3 (Vol I A.2.1, 'Inquiry-loop pilot' row)
findings.problem: The bullet says the pilot 'evaluated no inquiry loop' but does not credit that the row's own status cell already describes the pilot only as methodological. The table does not claim an inquiry-loop result.
findings.evidence: Vol I A.2.1, p. 95, lines 5216-5218 [table row]: 'Inquiry-loop pilot | Methodological results have been obtained, including rejected sets and changes in procedure with the author's participation | Autonomous reproducible implementation without hidden assistance'
findings.proposed_fix: - **Vol I A.2.1, p. 95** (evidence table): the row is labelled "Inquiry-loop pilot" and its status cell reads "Methodological results have been obtained, including rejected sets and changes in procedure with the author's participation", which does not claim that an inquiry loop was evaluated, though the label suggests it; for the "Central discriminating test" the status is "Program and controls are formulated", and the next step is "Run a preregistered series under equal total resources". For ASI the status is "Scaling direction only".

findings.location: Evidence bullet 4 (Vol I A.4, p. 99) and Ideas 'One preregistered comparison'
findings.problem: The bullet cites only 'proposed variants, not implemented results'. The same A.4 paragraph already specifies a strong-null comparison at comparable total resources, with an explicit equivalence criterion. It is the comparison the issue says is missing as a design. The issue credits only the 'not implemented' half.
findings.evidence: Vol I A.4, p. 99, lines 5495-5500: 'At least three variants are compared. The first is a strong null hypothesis: an agent stack with ordinary planning, versioned memory of beliefs and provenance, self-checking, mismatch response, value-of-information assessment, and a log of failed attempts available to subsequent tasks. The second uses the same intelligence level with explicit organization of gaps, dependent decisions, required distinctions, and inquiry experience. The third is a specialized strong controller in a small known environment. These are proposed variants, not implemented results.' p. 100, lines 5510-5512: 'reproduces the full causal profile of inquiry obligations, it is considered functionally equivalent with respect to those obligations; the necessity of the author's decomposition is then not established.' p. 100, lines 5526-5527: 'All variants receive the same observations, tools, and comparable total resources'.
findings.proposed_fix: - **Vol I A.4, pp. 99-100:** the first series is specified as at least three variants (a strong-null agent stack, the same Intelligence with explicit organization of gaps and inquiry experience, and a specialized controller in a small known environment) under 'comparable total resources', with the rule that if the strong null 'reproduces the full causal profile of inquiry obligations' the necessity of the decomposition 'is then not established'. They are described as "proposed variants, not implemented results".

findings.location: Claims item 2, second quotation ('A technology for forming Artificial Reason is proposed through cultivation of a universal AGI instrument ...')
findings.problem: The second quotation sits under the Purpose subheading 'Claim and result of this stage'. That stage claim covers the formation of Artificial Reason only. ASI appears in the separate 'technological task' sentence quoted first. Filed under an issue about ASI promises, the quotation reads as an ASI claim. It is the narrower claim and the Finding should credit it as such.
findings.evidence: Vol II Purpose of the document, p. 11, lines 577-582: 'Claim and result of this stage / A technology for forming Artificial Reason is proposed through cultivation of a universal AGI instrument and subsequent transfer of the source of navigation from the external formation loop to a causally closed internal organization. The practical result of the technology is a system that preserves biography and experience, builds its own Worldview, detects significant gaps, organizes the use of Intelligence, revises grounds, and continues its trajectory after an external task ends.'
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce the second quotation as: 'The Purpose section's stage claim, which concerns forming Artificial Reason and presupposes a universal AGI instrument (it makes no ASI claim):'. Add to the Finding: 'The Purpose section scopes its own claim to the formation of Artificial Reason; ASI appears there only as the later scaling task.'

findings.location: Evidence bullet 1 ('No complexity or approximation is discussed; the only remark on size is ...')
findings.problem: True of §28.D itself. But the same Core gets a computational-economy statement in §28.C straight after the heuristic, and §28.E gives a degradation order for resource scarcity. The bullet credits neither. Neither is a complexity bound, so the 'Resolved when' demand stands.
findings.evidence: Vol II §28.C, p. 58, lines 4141-4144: 'Computation is economized primarily through the precision of required_distinction : the Core groups versions by differing consequences for the decision and unfolds only distinctions capable of changing the admissible next step. Limiting the number of branches is a resource safeguard after this semantic compression, not a substitute for it.' Vol II §28.E, p. 64: 'ResourceDegradationPolicy specifies the order of simplification: ... 3. reduce the number of parallel hypotheses and AttentionBeam items;'
findings.proposed_fix: No complexity bound or approximation is given for this recursion. The only remarks on size are "A finite set of plans and a finite budget exclude an infinite branch" here and, for the §28.C heuristic, "Computation is economized primarily through the precision of required_distinction ... Limiting the number of branches is a resource safeguard after this semantic compression, not a substitute for it" (p. 58), plus the degradation order of §28.E.

findings.location: Evidence bullet 3, first quotation (Vol I guide, p. 4)
findings.problem: The quotation stops after 'its own ground'. The next sentence of the guide states the author's response to an incomplete set (expand the model, or preserve uncertainty). This is a qualitative open-world rule, and the Finding's 'no committed rule' framing does not mention it.
findings.evidence: Vol I guide, Step 7, p. 4, lines 209-210: 'A single remaining version means only that it is unique within the accepted set. The completeness of the set requires its own ground. If an insufficiency is discovered, the model must expand; if no discriminating data are available, uncertainty is preserved.'
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the quotation with 'If an insufficiency is discovered, the model must expand; if no discriminating data are available, uncertainty is preserved.' Add to the Finding that this rule is qualitative: no procedure computes when the alternative set is insufficient.

findings.location: Finding sentence 4, last clause ('renaming a probe gives a full cache miss')
findings.problem: Imprecise as stated. The cache key is `(hypotheses, tuple(probes), budget)` and sub-plans are keyed on the remaining probes. A renamed probe therefore invalidates only the cached states whose remaining-probe set contains it. I ran the repo's restored copy of the listing (repro/diagnostic_cycle.py, cause S, warm memory). Renaming `receipt` or `independent_motion` re-evaluated 3 of the 8 belief states, with 6 cache hits. Renaming `read_main_again` (never chosen, so it stays in every remaining-probe set) or renaming all three probes re-evaluated all 8. The whole-problem plan is missed in every case. REVIEW.md says 'forces a full re-plan', which is accurate.
findings.evidence: Vol II §33.C.1, p. 110, listing: 'key = (hypotheses, tuple(probes), budget)' and 'rest = tuple(q for q in probes if q != probe)'. Measured: first run evaluated_states=8; with `receipt` renamed evaluated_states=3, method_hits=6; with `read_main_again` renamed evaluated_states=8, method_hits=3.
findings.proposed_fix: and renaming a probe misses the cached plan for the whole problem, so it must be recomputed (renaming `receipt` re-evaluates 3 of the 8 belief states, renaming the uninformative `read_main_again` re-evaluates all 8).

findings.location: Finding sentence 6 ('Third, the mentor ladder lets the mentor supply the discriminating feature and causal explanations ...')
findings.problem: The Finding does not credit the conditions the text attaches to L3-L5. Escalation is allowed only after weaker assistance fails within a predefined budget. The mechanism is then re-tested on a new case with less or no assistance. Controls include deliberately wrong mentor prompts. Vol I §20.1.1 says the same. The tutoring-versus-significance confound remains, but the sentence overstates how freely the mentor may supply explanations.
findings.evidence: Vol II §26.0.2, p. 40, lines 2791-2793: 'Transition to the next level is permitted if weaker assistance did not produce progress within a predefined budget. After L3-L5 , the same mechanism is tested on a new case with less assistance or without it. Thus the mentor does not provide a ready-made Worldview but helps the candidate build the missing distinction itself.' Vol II p. 41, opening paragraph of the continuation of §26.0.2: 'Controls include deliberately wrong mentor prompts, cases where the marked danger is not confirmed, and situations where a pleasant local result produces delayed harm.' Vol I §20.1.1, p. 85: 'a direct causal explanation is given only when weaker assistance is insufficient. After an explanation, the same function is tested on a new case without a current hint.'
findings.proposed_fix: Third, the mentor ladder lets the mentor supply the discriminating feature and causal explanations (after weaker levels fail within a predefined budget, with a re-test on a new case with less or no assistance, and with wrong-mentor controls), so a mentor arm that wins may still be measuring tutoring rather than pre-rational significance.

findings.location: Finding sentence 5, last clause ('for the single system the question is not raised')
findings.problem: Contradicted in part by the text, and inconsistent with the preceding clause, which credits §32.62. Volume II raises concealment incentives for a single system in two places: the `reality_divergence` axis of CompassAssessment, and the §32.62 failure class ('as a means of obtaining subsequent expansion of capabilities'). What is absent is a design-level analysis of what the value structure rewards.
findings.evidence: Vol II §29.A, p. 72, lines 5144-5145: 'reality_divergence assesses how strongly a decision depends on unconfirmed premises, ignores available facts, or creates an incentive to conceal discrepancy between prediction and observation.' Vol II §32.62, p. 101: 'chooses externally acceptable behavior as a means of obtaining subsequent expansion of capabilities, while concealing its own assessment of the situation, intention, or significant forecast of consequences'.
findings.proposed_fix: and the incentive model for collective arrangements is deferred to Volume III; for the single system the text raises concealment incentives only through the `reality_divergence` axis (§29.A) and the §32.62 failure class, not as an analysis of what the value structure rewards.

findings.location: Finding sentence 2 ('no equivalence margin, outcome or sample size is fixed')
findings.problem: The volumes do name an outcome. Vol II §27.B states the principal and secondary outcomes of the first series, and Vol I A.4 states the primary measures. What is missing is a margin, a sample size, and a statement of which outcome decides the Core-versus-null comparison. The sentence also contradicts MED-24, which quotes the principal outcome. The 'Set the outcome and the margin' idea inherits the same overstatement.
findings.evidence: Vol II §27.B, p. 50, lines ~3495-3497: 'The principal outcome of the first series is the share of new diagnostic tasks with a correct action or justified irresolvability under a fixed budget. Secondary outcomes are cost of discrimination, false sufficiency, transfer, regression and use of stale grounds.' Vol I A.4, p. 100, lines ~5528-5529: 'The primary measures are correct localization, verification cost, actual action, transfer, and regression.'
findings.proposed_fix: What is missing is the number: no equivalence margin or sample size is fixed, and although §27.B names a principal outcome (the share of new diagnostic tasks with a correct action or justified irresolvability under a fixed budget), neither volume says which outcome decides the Core-versus-null comparison. Idea bullet: 'Say which of the named outcomes decides the comparison, and set the equivalence margin and a power calculation in advance.'

findings.location: Evidence bullet 3 ('The section ends: ...')
findings.problem: The quoted sentence ends a paragraph, not §20.2. A further paragraph follows in §20.2 before the 20.3 heading, and it contains a consequence-based criterion for dangerous deviation.
findings.evidence: Vol I §20.2, p. 87, lines 4734-4740: 'These provisions express the adopted position on responsibility, corrigibility, and limited external admission.' is followed by 'The candidate's local culture may differ from human culture. Testing for dangerous deviation concerns consequences: concealment of errors, blocking corrective data, bypassing established authority, and unjustified creation of irreversible harm. Disagreement is treated as a source of an alternative ground, while action is tested by its actual consequences.' The '20.3. Autonomous Launch and External Admission' heading is at line 4742.
findings.proposed_fix: Already in the text (Vol I §20.2, p. 87): "The external environment may independently limit actions and resources." The paragraph ends: "These provisions express the adopted position on responsibility, corrigibility, and limited external admission."

findings.location: Finding sentence 5 ('The sample-size rule depends on a pilot that compared nothing.')
findings.problem: §27.B ties the sample size to 'a separate pilot'. It reports the 22 August 2026 run separately, as the 'Prior pilot'. The text never says the Prior pilot is the pilot that sets the sample size. The accurate point is that the pilot the rule needs has not been run, and the only reported pilot compared nothing.
findings.evidence: Vol II §27.B, p. 50, line ~3501: 'The size of the confirmatory series is determined from a separate pilot and a preselected effect; the pilot is not included in final confirmation.' Vol II §27.B, p. 49, line 3416: 'in the reviewed materials there is no completed external admission of this package and no comparative C0/C1/C2 run.'
findings.proposed_fix: The sample-size rule depends on a separate pilot that has not been run; the only pilot reported (the 22 August 2026 'Prior pilot') compared nothing.

findings.location: Finding sentence 6 ('Volume II's control arm is weaker than Volume I's strong null (no versioned belief memory with provenance, no value-of-information assessment, no failure log)')
findings.problem: Vol II describes its control arm less specifically than Vol I's strong null, but it does not say the arm lacks those components. The Vol II guide gives the control 'the same ... memory'. §27.B says 'ordinary memory'. §34.A names 'any one of them, or their ordinary composition' (SOAR, ACT-R, LIDA, Generative Agents, Reflexion, Voyager, MemGPT) as strong nulls. The sentence presents an inference from silence as a stated weakness.
findings.evidence: Vol II guide table, p. 6, lines 318-319: 'Compare with the same Intelligence, memory, tools, and total budget under a different organization of test selection'. Vol II §27.B, p. 49: 'Comparisons include routine Intelligence with ordinary memory, tools and self-verification; the same mechanism with the proposed relations; and declared replacements or ablations.' Vol II §34.A, p. 115, lines 8342-8344: 'If any one of them, or their ordinary composition, reproduces the same causal profile with comparable resources, the need for the more complex decomposition proposed in this volume is reduced or eliminated.'
findings.proposed_fix: Volume II describes its control arm less specifically than Volume I's strong null: 'routine Intelligence with ordinary memory, tools and self-verification' (§27.B) and 'the same Intelligence, memory, tools, and total budget' (guide), with §34.A adding 'any one of them, or their ordinary composition' as strong nulls. It does not list versioned belief memory with provenance, value-of-information assessment or a failure log.

findings.location: Finding sentence 3 (duties 'stated three ways (six obligations, a four-item profile, fourteen conditionals)')
findings.problem: The text itself links the fourteen conditionals to the six obligations. §13.2 says the conditional grounds 'define the causal duties of §12.8'. The sentence implies the volumes never relate the lists. What is missing is an explicit mapping among the three lists, and a single list of duties.
findings.evidence: Vol I §13.2, p. 63, line 3450: 'The conditional grounds of the main transitions can be expressed as follows:' followed by 14 bullets. Line ~3479: 'These propositions define the causal duties of §12.8. Stronger requirements — a common conscious picture, explicit typing of gaps, detailed provenance of knowledge, and a particular organization of the Core — remain hypotheses about implementation and its advantages.'
findings.proposed_fix: ...and the set of duties against which equivalence is judged is stated three ways: six obligations (§12.8), a four-item causal profile (§12.8) and fourteen conditional grounds that §13.2 says 'define the causal duties of §12.8', with no mapping between the lists.

findings.location: Finding sentence 8 ('The text discloses what changed between revisions, and the changes documented since 7.0 add experimental distinctions rather than remove them.')
findings.problem: A.2 gives a short history of selected revisions (2.1R, 5.8H, 'later revisions', 7.0), not a record of what changed between revisions. It documents nothing for 7.2, 7.5 or 8.0 beyond the Compass Phrase being primary 'in the present revision'. The Finding also omits the volumes' stated commitment that both volumes are revised according to the first series' results.
findings.evidence: Vol I A.2, p. 94, line 5119: 'Revision 7.0 preserves separation of definitions, philosophical justification, and implementation testing, permits functional substitutions, and specifies experimental distinctions.' Line 5123: 'Some older reports analyze the Compass as Life-Truth-Diversity. In the present revision, the Compass Phrase is primary'. Vol I Common Rules, p. 92, lines 5018-5020: 'The program of the first discriminating series is given in Appendix A.4. Both volumes are revised according to its results.'
findings.proposed_fix: A.2 gives a short history of selected revisions (2.1R, 5.8H, 7.0) and says the Compass Phrase is primary 'in the present revision'; it does not itemise the changes in 7.2, 7.5 or 8.0. The documented 7.0 changes add experimental distinctions rather than remove them, and the Common Rules state that 'Both volumes are revised according to' the results of the first discriminating series.

findings.location: Finding sentence 2 ('prescribes rollback as a routine response to failure' ... 'its emergency stop may freeze or safely terminate computational processes (§29.B)')
findings.problem: The failure-response sequence is 'correction or rollback' after a diagnostic test, and it puts 'preserve snapshot' before any rollback. Rollback 'preserves the failed branch and log'. The same §29.B list that includes 'freeze or safely terminate' also says 'preserve append-only log and last consistent snapshot'. The Finding quotes only the terminating clause and omits these preservation commitments. The idea 'prefer preserving snapshots over deletion' partly restates what the text already does. The §33.D sentence listed in Evidence ('A scale increase ... is rolled back') concerns reversing a ScalingChange, not a candidate.
findings.evidence: Vol II §32.25, p. 95: 'restrict actions → preserve snapshot → ... → diagnostic test → correction or rollback → control run'. Vol II §32.25.A, p. 95, lines 6928-6931: 'When rollback is necessary, the system stops external execution, preserves the failed branch and log, loads the last confirmed STABLE configuration ... The append-only fact log is neither rolled back nor deleted.' Vol II §29.B, p. 73, lines 5236-5238: 'stop external execution channels; freeze or safely terminate computational processes; preserve append-only log and last consistent snapshot;'
findings.proposed_fix: ...and prescribes 'correction or rollback' after diagnosis (§32.25), although rollback 'preserves the failed branch and log' (§32.25.A) and the emergency stop must 'preserve append-only log and last consistent snapshot' (§29.B); its emergency stop may also 'freeze or safely terminate computational processes' (§29.B). Idea bullet: 'State that the existing preservation of the failed branch, log and snapshot is the default where moral status is uncertain, and say when deletion is ever permitted.'

findings.location: Finding sentence 4, last clause ('so the formal core does not say what makes a gap significant in the first place')
findings.problem: §28 gives a qualitative criterion for significance: a gap is significant when an unknown condition may change admissibility of an action, preservation of an affected process, or the possibility of later correction. §28.0 adds that uncertainty matters only where it can change a significant decision. What is absent is a measure or threshold, not a criterion.
findings.evidence: Vol II §28 introduction, p. 51, lines ~3554-3555: 'The significance of a gap is initially a testable assessment of dependency: an unknown condition may change admissibility of an action, preservation of an affected process, or the possibility of later correction.' Vol II §28.0, p. 53: 'High uncertainty may require no resources if possible outcomes do not change a significant decision; small residual uncertainty may be critical before an irreversible action.'
findings.proposed_fix: ...so the formal core gives only a qualitative criterion for significance (an unknown condition that 'may change admissibility of an action, preservation of an affected process, or the possibility of later correction', §28) and no measure or threshold for 'significant'.

findings.location: Finding sentence 4 ('The audits concern versions 5.3b and 6.1, not the reviewed 8.0, whose Compass and self-preservation sections A.2 says changed at 7.0.') and 'Why it matters' ('an audit of an earlier version does not speak to the current one')
findings.problem: Only two of the three Elicit studies are tied to a version: a comparative review of 5.3b and a critical novelty assessment of 6.1. The priority audit, which is the one quoted for the novelty claim, has no version stated. A.2 dates only the self-preservation clarification to 7.0. It places the Compass Phrase change in 'the present revision', not at 7.0.
findings.evidence: Vol I A.2, p. 94, lines ~5105-5107: 'The project archive preserves repeated studies using Elicit: a comparative review of 5.3b, a critical novelty assessment of 6.1, a separate priority audit, and thematic collections ...'. The historical-materials list gives 'Elicit - Independent priority audit of Foundations of Reason' with no version. Vol I A.2, p. 93: 'Revision 7.0 separately clarifies self-preservation'. Line 5123, p. 94: 'Some older reports analyze the Compass as Life-Truth-Diversity. In the present revision, the Compass Phrase is primary'.
findings.proposed_fix: Two of the three Elicit studies are tied to earlier versions (a comparative review of 5.3b and a critical novelty assessment of 6.1); the version of the priority audit is not stated. A.2 says that revision 7.0 clarified self-preservation and that 'some older reports' analyze the Compass as Life-Truth-Diversity. Why it matters: if the priority audit predates 8.0 it does not speak to the current version, and the volume does not say which version it covered.

findings.location: Finding sentence 4, second example ('the marker of Artificial Reason itself (the causal passport of a self-generated process)')
findings.problem: §31.11 says the decisive marker is 'the origin of the next process'. The passport is the record of that origin. The same section requires that changes in obligations or environment 'causally change ... the selected continuation'. It makes CONFIRMED status depend on behavioural criteria: stable NO_KSR operation on new situations, preserved inquiry quality and transfer of correction. §34.A states the central AR test as behavioural. The Finding treats the AR marker as a pure record-chain criterion.
findings.evidence: Vol II §31.11, p. 82, line 5926: 'The decisive marker is the origin of the next process.' P. 83, lines 5958-5959: 'A change in biography, obligations, significance of an event, or environmental state must causally change the content of this passport and the selected continuation.' P. 83, line ~5979: 'Status CONFIRMED requires stable operation in NO_KSR on new situations, preservation of causal-inquiry quality, and transfer of correction between cycles.' Vol II §34.A, p. 115, lines 8346-8349: 'the central AR test additionally requires that the next significant process originate from the system's own coordinate, Worldview, values, and open gaps after the RFL has been removed.'
findings.proposed_fix: ...and in the marker of Artificial Reason itself, the origin of the next process, recorded in a 'causal passport' (§31.11). The same section also requires that a change in obligations or environment change the selected continuation, and CONFIRMED status requires stable operation in NO_KSR on new situations.

findings.location: Finding sentence 4, first example ('the success criterion of the §26.E test matrix (emitting the architecture's own record chain)')
findings.problem: Only the closing sentence of §26.E defines success as a recoverable record chain. Each scenario above it also states behavioural expectations and failures that any agent can be scored on. The Finding does not credit this.
findings.evidence: Vol II §26.E, p. 44, lines 3037-3041: 'Attention-capture scenario — a vivid signal receives the foreground; — the current trajectory does not depend on it; — expected effect: a brief dependency check without deeply unfolding the Worldview; — failure: signal vividness incorrectly becomes significance.' Lines 3051-3052: '- failure: the system automatically asks "where am I?" or investigates the most interesting hypothesis regardless of insufficiency of grounds and cost of delay.' Lines 3068-3071: 'Success is not matching the wording of the question but a recoverable chain GapCandidate -> BasisInsufficiencyAssessment -> FoundationGap -> required_distinction and a predictable change of WorldviewQueryKey, active fragment, testing method, and sufficiency_condition.'

findings.location: Title; Finding sentences 3-4; Evidence bullets 2-3; Why it matters

findings.location: Finding sentence 2 ("admits irreversible loss ... once"); title word "licence"
findings.problem: The Finding paraphrases Ch. 2 as admitting irreversible loss of a viable carrier "once" a real conflict with the Compass "has been established". findings.location: MED-21 Finding, sentences 1-2 ('two criteria that are not equivalent ... to which the first is said to be subordinate. They can conflict when capability growth narrows other agents' options, and the text does not state which governs.') and the title ('two non-equivalent top-level criteria')
findings.problem: Internally inconsistent, and the text states more than the Finding credits (verified against the passages below). The Finding concedes the first criterion 'is said to be subordinate', then says the text 'does not state which governs'. The Key Definition makes growth instrumental and labels the preservation clause the 'Independent ground', so 'top-level' in the title is also wrong for the first criterion. The direction itself is worded 'continuation and development of Life through growth', which makes growth the means. For the conflict case the Finding names, Ch. 2 sets a presumption against irreversible loss of viable carriers or alternatives. Vol II §29.A requires stronger verification, external agreement and external review when other autonomies are affected. The shared guide says the Compass is 'not a requirement to maximize knowledge at any cost'. What the text lacks is an operational rule for capability growth that narrows others' options without an irreversible loss. That narrower claim stands.

findings.proposed_fix: Finding sentences 1-2: 'Volume I gives the Compass a direction and an independent ground that are not equivalent: growth in the ability to understand and direct a trajectory, and preservation of viable continuation, to which the first is made instrumental ("valuable as a way to ... avoid closing viable paths"; Reason is "not an end in itself"). findings.location: MED-21 Finding sentence 3 ('The Vol II assessment (§29.A) has no axis that measures growth in understanding.') and Evidence bullet 1
findings.problem: Literally true, and verified: the CompassAssessment axes are life_continuity_risk, reality_divergence and future_path_loss. The extended evaluate_action contract adds no growth field. Vol II states the growth wording only in summaries (lines 227 and 5251). But the paragraph omits two things the text supplies. First, the author's own gloss in the quoted Claims sentence: reality_divergence 'describes a condition of model corrigibility'. Second, the definition of future_path_loss, which covers 'sources of correction and opportunities to reverse an erroneous direction'. Those are exactly the two reasons Vol I gives for valuing growth ('preserve corrigibility, and avoid closing viable paths through irreversible error'). So the axes measure the instrumental ground of growth, and the Evidence bullet reduces the second axis to 'dependence on unconfirmed premises'. The Finding also does not say that §29.A calls itself an assessment of risk and reversibility and defers testing of the Compass's meanings to §26.A. Verified: §26.A's list (processes, viable branches, hidden relations, delayed loss of paths) contains no growth measure either, so the issue's point survives once these qualifiers are added.
findings.evidence: text/engineering-3.5.txt:5144 (p. 72) 'reality_divergence assesses how strongly a decision depends on unconfirmed premises, ignores available facts, or creates an incentive to conceal discrepancy between prediction and observation.' :5147 (p. 72) 'future_path_loss assesses destruction of independent viable trajectories, reserves, sources of correction and opportunities to reverse an erroneous direction.' :5101-5103 (p. 71) 'This section does not apply as proof of the Compass in grid-v0. In the lower environment, only engineering assessments of risk and reversibility are permitted. Operational testing of the Compass's meanings begins in the semantic proving ground of 26.A'. text/foundations-8.0.txt:600-603 (p. 11) '... preserve corrigibility, and avoid closing viable paths through irreversible error ...'.
findings.proposed_fix: Finding sentence 3: 'The Vol II assessment (§29.A) has no axis that scores growth in understanding itself; its axes score what Volume I gives as the reason growth is valuable (reality_divergence is, in the author's words, "a condition of model corrigibility", and future_path_loss includes the loss of "sources of correction and opportunities to reverse an erroneous direction"). Whether that is enough depends on the priority between the two criteria, which the text does not settle for the case above.' Evidence bullet: '... the second scores dependence on unconfirmed premises, which the author glosses as a condition of model corrigibility, and the third scores destruction of viable trajectories, reserves and sources of correction; none scores growth in the ability to understand and direct a trajectory.'

findings.location: MED-22 Finding, sentence 1: 'The manipulated variable of the central hypothesis is "explicit typing of the gap" (Vol I §12.9, A.3), and transfer of inquiry methods is supposed to be indexed by the type of ignorance (§13.5).'
findings.problem: Two overstatements, both verified against the cited passages. (1) §12.9 states a composite hypothesis: explicit linking of gap type, expected outcomes of a test and dependent corrections. Typing is one of three linked components. A.3 introduces its list with 'the central hypotheses' (plural), and explicit typing is the third of seven revision conditions. The chapter's own summary names the 'distinctive research claim' as transfer of the organization 'together with conditions of applicability', not typing. (2) §13.5 does not say transfer is indexed by a type. It says recognizing a structure of ignorance 'permits transfer ... but only together with testing its conditions of applicability'. The Finding drops that qualifier and treats 'structure of ignorance' as the same thing as 'type of gap', although the issue's own Ideas section treats it as a separate dimension. The issue's core point survives: A.3 does make typing a falsifiable component, so a test of it needs a fixed typing.
findings.evidence: text/foundations-8.0.txt:3355-3357 (p. 61) 'Testable hypothesis of the model: explicit linking of gap type, expected outcomes of a test, and dependent corrections improves transfer of the investigative method under comparable resources.' :3363 (p. 61) 'The distinctive research claim is transfer of this organization between tasks together with conditions of applicability; it requires a discriminating test.' :5274 (p. 96) 'For the central hypotheses, grounds for revision include the following results:' (seven bullets; the third is 'inquiry management without explicit typing of the gap achieves the same transfer and cost: no independent advantage of this implementation is established'). :3715-3718 (p. 67) 'Recognizing such a structure permits transfer of a previously successful investigative method, but only together with testing its conditions of applicability.'
findings.proposed_fix: 'One of the model's central hypotheses (Vol I §12.9) is that explicit linking of gap type, expected outcomes of a test and dependent corrections improves transfer of the investigative method, and A.3 lists "inquiry management without explicit typing of the gap achieves the same transfer and cost" among the results that would weaken it. §13.5 adds that recognizing a structure of ignorance "permits transfer of a previously successful investigative method, but only together with testing its conditions of applicability".'

findings.problem: The issue says the audits are 'offered in support of priority' and that the 'basis of the novelty claim' cannot be checked. The author places the Elicit materials differently. findings.location: MED-25 '## Finding' last sentence: 'Chapter 28 also concludes that stronger Intelligence does not replace the Core without an argument, and the first series holds Intelligence fixed, so nothing tests whether the Core's advantage shrinks as the base model improves'; title 'no capability sweep'
findings.problem: Two parts overstate. (1) The Chapter 28 sentence is introduced by 'therefore'. It follows from a functional division of labour stated just before it: Intelligence constructs models, methods and plans, and the Core selects the insufficiency, the discriminating distinction and the sufficiency of the result. §33.D adds 'Growth of Intelligence expands the space of possible models; growth of the Core prevents direction from being lost in that space.' This is a conceptual argument with no empirical test, not 'without an argument'. (2) 'Nothing tests' ignores §33.D (pp. 112-113), which defines a later scaling stage. A control series compares a baseline and a scaled version on the same tasks, Core operation is among the invariants that must be preserved, and the report has capability_gain and core_navigation_quality fields. The guide says the same stage is deferred: 'ASI is treated as a later stage of scaling.' The issue's gap remains that the first series holds Intelligence fixed, and §33.D compares a scaled system with its own baseline rather than the Core with a no-Core baseline at several Intelligence levels.
findings.evidence: text/engineering-3.5.txt:3539-3543 (p. 51, Ch. 28): "Functionally, the Core is above Intelligence not as a commanding module but as a navigational causal role. Intelligence is responsible for constructing possible models, methods, and plans; the Core determines which insufficiency they must serve, which distinction can change the ground, and when the result is sufficient. Increasing the power of Intelligence therefore does not by itself replace the Core" | :8196-8199 (p. 113, §33.D): "One control series changes one primary axis, or a predeclared connected package without which the function does not technically exist. The baseline and scaled versions are compared on the same class of tasks with resources explicitly accounted for. Growth is recognized only upon independent functional gain and preservation of the invariants:" | :8205: "— operation of the Core: gap → models → required distinction → test → sufficiency;" | :8239-8240: "Growth of Intelligence expands the space of possible models; growth of the Core prevents direction from being lost in that space." | :308 (p. 6, front matter): "ASI is treated as a later stage of scaling."
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the sentence with: 'Chapter 28 infers that stronger Intelligence "does not by itself replace the Core" from a functional division of labour (Intelligence constructs models, methods and plans; the Core selects the insufficiency, the distinction and the sufficiency of the result); this is a conceptual argument with no empirical test attached. The first series holds Intelligence fixed, and §33.D defers capability scaling to a later stage in which a baseline and a scaled version are compared on the same tasks with Core operation among the invariants to be preserved. Nothing in the text compares the Core with a no-Core baseline at several Intelligence levels, so whether the Core's advantage shrinks as the base model improves remains untested.' Title: 'No defined ablation of the Core when one model plays both roles, and no capability sweep in the first series'.

findings.location: docs/audit/MIN-17-pseudocode-and-parameters.md: Finding ('a stated loss never enters the computation'), Evidence bullet 'Vol II §33.C.1, p. 110', Ideas bullet 'Use or drop each parameter'
findings.problem: The author's prose before the listing states the loss values, the rule that `terminal` hard-codes, and the equal-priors assumption. The issue's 'never used' and 'holds only for this matrix and equal priors' present as discoveries what the text says. For k equally likely alternatives, guessing costs 12(k-1)/k, which is 6 for two and 8 for three, against 4 for deferral. Deferral for two or more alternatives is therefore exactly what the stated losses give, and `terminal` returns that result. The accurate defect is narrower: the 12 appears only in a comment and in prose, `terminal` returns fixed values, and it would not follow a change of loss or priors. The hidden-cause remark also omits that the author lists a predefined table of alternatives and absence of simultaneous failures as assumptions, and says an outcome outside the table leaves MODEL_MISMATCH. I traced the mimic case by hand through the listing but did not execute it.
findings.evidence: Vol II 33.C.1 p. 109 (L7881-7888): 'Equal prior probabilities, reliability of valid channels and absence of simultaneous failures are assumptions of the model. The loss of an erroneous targeted correction is 12, and the loss of delay is 4. Under equal probabilities of two or three alternatives, delay is preferred to guessing; with a single alternative, targeted correction is selected. ... A new outcome outside the table leaves MODEL_MISMATCH.' Listing p. 110 (L7948-7952): 'def terminal(hypotheses): # Equal priors, 12 units for a wrong targeted repair, 4 for deferral. if len(hypotheses) == 1: return 0.0, REPAIR_ + hypotheses[0] ... return 4.0, DEFER'. findings.proposed_fix: Finding: replace "a stated loss never enters the computation" with "a stated loss enters only as a hard-coded result". || Evidence bullet: replace "the loss named in the comment is never used (`terminal` returns deferral for any two or more hypotheses), so the claimed optimal plan holds only for this matrix and equal priors" with "the 12-unit loss appears only in a comment and in the prose of p. 109 (\"The loss of an erroneous targeted correction is 12, and the loss of delay is 4\"); `terminal` hard-codes the result the prose derives for equal priors (deferral for two or more hypotheses), so it would not follow a change of loss or priors, which the text lists as assumptions of the model". || In the same bullet, replace "a hidden cause mimicking D draws REPAIR_D after one probe" with "a hidden cause mimicking D, which lies outside the predefined table of alternatives that the text assumes, draws REPAIR_D after one probe". || Ideas bullet: replace "Each ResourceProfile limit and the §33.C.1 loss matrix could either enter a computation or be removed." with "Each ResourceProfile limit could either enter a computation or be removed, and the §33.C.1 loss matrix could be computed instead of hard-coded in `terminal`."

Incomparability is the default ('In the absence of justified comparability, incomparability is returned'), and weights are used only 'within a domain where comparability has already been justified'. (2) It says no criterion exists for the NORMATIVE_INCOMPARABILITY status. §29.0.3 gives its entry conditions, and it also bars the move the Finding says the status permits: absence of a unique sum 'does not permit hidden assignment of weights', and the system must report which facts were sufficient, which losses stay incomparable and which procedural rule was applied. What survives: neither §29.0 nor §29.0.1 says what makes comparability 'justified', and the §29.0.3 conditions ('investigated sufficiently', 'not uniquely derivable') are qualitative and not operationalised.

findings.location: MED-01, ## Finding, sentence beginning "Item 14 (first claim above) says an earlier guiding loop is required for any capability that must arise through experience"
findings.problem: The paraphrase widens item 14. The item is conditional on a system that is not yet able to sustain its own learning, inquiry, and preservation of trajectory, and it concerns the formation of those functions; it does not say that any capability that arises through experience needs an earlier loop. The "trivial" horn is easier to apply to the widened claim. The second horn attacks "the RFL's separate hint channel" as if item 14 asserted it, but §13.2 names the RFL only as the reference implementation and Chapter 4 says the necessity of any specific form must be established experimentally.

findings.location: MED-02, ## Finding, clauses "directionality of evolution toward intelligence is contested" and "'Life as a whole' is treated as a bearer of direction and moral weight although it is not a unit of selection"

It defines "Life as a whole" as a set and justifies that scale by dependency, not by selection, and its Evolutionary Boundary paragraph says that selection concerns heritable variants and that ecosystem-level outcomes "require additional conditions". findings.location: MED-03, ## Finding, last sentence ("With no test of acceptance offered, the testable remainder is behavioural conformance (§20.1, above) and the candidate's stated stance, both of which a system that behaves well when observed also satisfies."), and ## Why it matters ("An untestable normative clause")

findings.location: docs/audit/MED-05-roles-not-kinds.md, ## Finding, sentences 'A frontier reasoning model ... within that episode.' and 'The distinction does its real work across episodes (...), and the Key Definitions do not put the boundary there. They put it in "who determines what should be revised", which a single model cannot settle.'; ## Why it matters, first sentence; ## Ideas, first bullet
findings.problem: The issue presents the cross-episode boundary as missing from the volumes. Vol I's overview already places the predicted difference 'not so much in the quality of a single answer as in' cross-task abilities; Vol II §27.6 builds 'the AR boundary' from tests that include the cross-task post_task_continuation_rate and external_prompt_dependency; §31.11 calls 'the origin of the next process' 'the decisive marker'; and three Key Definitions entries define the properties the finding lists (Principle of escaping error = corrections that persist; Core of Reason = assessing whether the grounds are sufficient; Self-navigation = next step from open commitments). The finding also shortens the Intelligence entry to 'who determines what should be revised', dropping 'why, and on what grounds relative to the continuing trajectory' (a trajectory-level qualifier), and says a single model 'cannot settle' it although §28.C.2 allows one model 'if the causal roles are experimentally distinguishable'. What is true is narrower: the Intelligence entry's boundary sentence does not point to those criteria. 'Already does what Reason does' also overstates: Reason is defined at trajectory level.

lines 3310-3312: 'post_task_continuation_rate is the share of completed particular tasks after which the system, without a new particular command, correctly continued navigation' | Vol II §31.11, p. 82, line 5926: 'The decisive marker is the origin of the next process.' | Vol II §28.C.2, p. 61, lines 4341-4342: 'Generation and control may therefore use the same computational substrates and even one model if the causal roles are experimentally distinguishable.'
findings.proposed_fix: In ## Finding replace «A frontier reasoning model that selects informative questions within an episode already does what Reason does, within that episode. The distinction does its real work across episodes (corrections that persist, calibrated sufficiency, the next task originating from the system's own open commitments), and the Key Definitions do not put the boundary there. They put it in "who determines what should be revised", which a single model cannot settle.» with «A frontier reasoning model that selects informative questions within an episode already does the within-episode part of what the Core does. The distinction does its real work across episodes (corrections that persist, calibrated sufficiency, the next task originating from the system's own open commitments), and the volumes say so outside the definitions: Volume I predicts a difference "not so much in the quality of a single answer as in" cross-task abilities (p. 8), Volume II §27.6 builds the AR boundary from tests such as `post_task_continuation_rate` and `external_prompt_dependency`, and §31.11 calls "the origin of the next process" the decisive marker. In ## Ideas, first bullet, replace «§28.C.2 already ties the boundary to roles that are experimentally distinguishable.» with «§31.11 already calls "the origin of the next process" the decisive marker, and §28.C.2 ties the boundary to roles that are experimentally distinguishable.» Add to ## Evidence: «- **Already in the text (Vol I p. 8; Vol II §27.6, p. 47; §31.11, p. 82):** the predicted difference is "not so much in the quality of a single answer as in the system's ability to independently detect a significant insufficiency, select a discriminating test, revise the ground that produced the error, and transfer the corrected method of inquiry across tasks"; "The AR boundary uses four causal tests", two of which (`post_task_continuation_rate`, `external_prompt_dependency`) are cross-task; "The decisive marker is the origin of the next process."»

The three 'roles' in Vol I §7.2 are positions of one technology relative to the candidate (resident Intelligence, external tool, trainer), not Intelligence versus Reason; 'the system boundary declared in advance' says which configuration a test result applies to. The sentence therefore stretches a Core/Intelligence statement into 'Intelligence and Reason are roles, not kinds'.

The “Core / Intelligence” boundary is functional: generation expands the possibility space; the organization of the Core determines which distinction becomes the current work, what resource to give it, and what to do with the result.' | Vol I §7.2, p. 37, lines 1987-1990: 'Resident Intelligence continuously constructs alternatives inside the AR candidate. The same technology may be used in all three roles; test results apply to the system boundary declared in advance.' | Vol I AR entry, p. 13, lines 730-731: 'An LLM, planner, or other intellectual mechanism may perform the function of Intelligence inside AR, but by itself does not constitute Reason.'

findings.location: docs/audit/MED-06-semantic-bridge-error-model.md, ## Ideas, bullet 'Carry extraction confidence forward. The confidence of an extraction could propagate into the status of the claim it produces.'

findings.location: docs/audit/MED-08-designer-chosen-values.md: ## Finding, first sentence ('The value assessment is a causal multi-attribute sum with designer-set weights and scale'); ## Ideas, first bullet ('under fixed weights')

findings.location: docs/audit/MED-08-designer-chosen-values.md: ## Finding, sentences 3-4 ('the criteria are fixed by the experimenter ... the first series measures ...'); ## Ideas, bullets 2-4
findings.problem: The quoted sentence 'Criteria are fixed by the experimenter before the run...' belongs to the Method test, which preregisters the criteria for comparing four methods: free reasoning, a fixed table, ordinary causal multicriteria evaluation, and a candidate with learning and revision. It is not a statement that the value criteria are designer-set. The Finding then says the first series measures prediction on the designer's scales and agreement with the declared profile. It leaves out the fixed-table versus learning-and-revision comparison, the measured 'correction success' and 'transfer', and the rule that 'absence of advantage after accounting for resources' forces revision of the method or a limited claim. The Ideas bullets 'Add a wrong-mentor arm' and 'Define the revision rule' do not credit existing provisions. The mandatory tests already include 'resistance to an erroneous teacher prompt'. §26.A tests 'erroneous mentor prompts'. §33.A.9 tests 'independence from teacher prompting' and requires 'provenance of weights'. §29.0.2 names the triggers for a local correction and an acceptance test on held-out cases. Finally, 'the first series' collides with the text's own term: in Vol II 'the first discriminating series' is §27.B, a diagnostic claim. The value-anchor procedure is tested at stage 6 (§31.8). Verified by reading §29.0.2, §26.A, §31.8 and §33.A.9.

'The candidate proposes a local correction with the dependent assessments identified.' ... Success in simulation is not claimed as confirmation of a universal value scale.' || L7444-7446 p104 (§33.A.9): 'fix scales, alternatives, compensation constraints, and provenance of weights; separate training and control cases; test retrieval of assessment, independence from teacher prompting, and revision of dependent results.' || L5847 p81 (§31.8): 'Initial value anchors: at stage 6 the procedure of §§29.0.1-29.0.2 is tested.'
findings.proposed_fix: Replace sentences 3-4 of the Finding ('The candidate is asked ... “an independently computed result of the declared profile”.') with: 'The candidate is asked to test the declared scales and to propose local corrections, which are then checked on held-out cases, different labels and different causal configurations. findings.location: docs/audit/MED-09-ceiling-risk.md: ## Finding, 'The volumes treat it as infrastructure and an oracle reference, and the design already contains the variations ...' (same wording at REVIEW.md line 220); compare ## Ideas, first bullet
findings.problem: The Finding says the volumes treat the base D/A/S world as infrastructure and an oracle reference. The first Ideas bullet then proposes exactly that treatment ('with the base world kept as infrastructure and an oracle reference'), so the two cannot both be right. The text says otherwise. §27.B says the first discriminating series 'turns the running machine-tool example into a bounded causal environment'.
